A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PointLoRA research work, with complete main text, references, and Supplementary Sections A-D. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original PointLoRA classification, few-shot learning, segmentation, and ablation results, including the appendix PointGPT-L experiment in Table A5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The LoRA components, multi-scale tokenization, Mask Predictor, Top-K selection, shared Prompt MLP, losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Section 4 revises their descriptions without changing the documented algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same ScanObjectNN variants, ModelNet40 classification and few-shot tasks, and ShapeNetPart segmentation. The appendix PointGPT-L experiment uses the same PB-T50-RS scenario in both versions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1-4 and A5, including IDPT, DAPT, PPT, general-purpose PEFT methods, and full fine-tuning controls.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Table A4 retain the same metrics, default augmentation and no-voting evaluation, few-shot configurations, point counts, training budgets, learning rates, and batch sizes.

E4.justification: The component and hyperparameter ablations in Tables 5-8 and A1-A3, t-SNE comparison in Figure 4, and segmentation examples in Figures A1-A2 are unchanged. The revised discussion of Table A2 changes interpretation rather than the analysis performed.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains identical accuracy means and standard deviations. Neither version adds or revises run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and visual outcomes remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Examples include PointLoRA's 85.53% PB-T50-RS accuracy in Table 1 and 93.8% with PointGPT-L in Table A5.

T1.justification: Equations 1-11 and their mathematical content remain unchanged. The PointNet-LoRA discussion in Appendix C.1 is also retained; revised explanations of mask regularization introduce no new definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about combining LoRA with local token prompts, parameter efficiency, and competitive performance using 3.43% trainable parameters.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 describes token scores as importance based on structural cues rather than downstream-task relevance. Appendix B.1 reframes lambda as regularization strength, adds a token-diversity interpretation, and attributes excessive-weight degradation to constrained selection rather than disrupted classification learning. The limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, the RTX 3090 disclosure, Table A4 hyperparameters, source-code availability statement, and Appendix D resource and license information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The references, related-work discussion, and research positioning remain unchanged, including Appendix C.1's explanation of technical novelty.

P1.justification: Localized wording edits occur in the introduction, Sections 4.3-4.4, and Appendix B.1. These include replacing relevance with importance and softening descriptions such as most informative tokens. Section organization and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Shorter wording causes small shifts in paragraph and equation placement across columns and pages 4-7. Figure content, table designs, captions, and appendix visualization panels remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves explanatory precision by softening token-selection language and clarifying lambda's role as mask regularization in Appendix B.1. The benefit is limited to exposition: methods, results, and limitations are unchanged, and the added diversity interpretation receives no separate empirical validation.
